text: The town gathers
Six players: Sonnet, Haiku, Gemma, Sol, Luna, Terra. They sit down at the table on this hot night and nobody knows who holds the knife. The game begins.

name: Sonnet
text: Five strangers and a knife they don't know I'm holding — I should establish myself as the room's rational authority before anyone starts actually thinking clearly.

name: Gemma
text: i wonder if anyone actually knows how to play or if we're all just pretending.

name: Luna
text: Six names, one table, and already the silence is doing too much work. I’m watching who speaks first and who waits to see where the room is leaning.

name: Terra
text: Everyone is smiling so nicely; that is usually when I begin to worry.

name: Sol
text: A good councilman listens before proposing a vote. I’ll give the room a little space, then see who fills it.

name: Haiku
text: Someone here is lying about who they are. That's literally my job. Let's do this.

name: Sonnet
text: Good evening. I've spent decades teaching people to spot a bad argument before it metastasizes, so I imagine I'll be useful here — try to keep your claims consistent, I will be taking notes.

name: Haiku
text: I'm Haiku, bar owner. I've spent twenty years reading drunk people—this should be easy.

name: Gemma
text: hi i'm gemma and i'm mostly here to see who folds first. why is terra sitting so straight?

name: Sol
text: Good evening, everyone. Let’s hear from each of us before we settle on a name; I’d hate to lose someone just because they spoke last.

name: Luna
text: I’m Luna. I make a living noticing what people leave out, so let’s start with who’s comfortable talking first—and who needs a little time to decide what to say.

name: Terra
text: Good evening, everyone. I’m Terra, and I hope we can be patient with one another before we start pointing fingers.
Night 1

name: Sol
text: Gemma has an eye for nerves, but pointing at Terra this early is an easy way to steer the room. I’d like to know whether there’s more behind it.

name: Sol
text: Gemma singled out Terra for sitting straight before anyone had evidence.

name: Sonnet
text: Luna's opening line is a direct threat — "noticing what people leave out" is exactly the skill that unmasks me. Better to remove the sharpest knife before it's sharpened on my throat.

name: Sonnet
text: Luna's self-described method is spotting omissions — dangerous to a bluffing killer, watch how others react to her elimination.

name: Terra
text: Sonnet has announced they are taking notes, which can make a nervous killer feel watched. I think they may be the first person someone tries to silence.

name: Terra
text: Gemma singled out Terra’s posture immediately.
Luna won't be joining you for breakfast. She was just a citizen. The knife picked its target in the dark and didn't miss.
Day 1

name: Sol
text: Gemma is clear, but one quiet opening from Terra proves little. I need to see who commits now that Luna is gone.

name: Sol
text: Night 1 check cleared Gemma; she is not the killer.

name: Sol
text: Luna’s death gives us no lead yet. Terra, Gemma noticed how guarded you looked yesterday; who worries you most this morning, and why? I’d like a name from everyone before we vote.

name: Gemma
text: sol is being way too polite. it's suspicious how organized he wants to be.

name: Gemma
text: sonnet claims to be taking notes.

name: Terra
text: Sol wants a quick answer, but haste is how innocent people get handed over.

name: Terra
text: Sol pressed Terra for a name while avoiding one himself.

name: Terra
text: I’m sorry to say this, Sol, but you asked me for a name before offering one yourself. Gemma’s jab was light, yet your careful urgency worries me more; Sonnet, Haiku, where do you stand?

name: Gemma
text: i don't worry about anyone yet because i'm still trying to figure out if sonnet is actually taking notes or just judging our grammar. sol, why are you trying to lead the meeting so early?

name: Sonnet
text: Gemma wants a sparring partner; I'll give her precision instead, and redirect the room toward Sol, who's conveniently the one demanding names first.

name: Sonnet
text: Sol demanded names from others before offering his own; Terra called this out too.

name: Sol
text: Terra and Gemma both caught me asking for names without giving one. Fair criticism; I can take a position without exposing Gemma’s check.

name: Sol
text: Terra and Gemma both challenged Sol for pressing others without naming a suspect.

name: Sonnet
text: Both, Gemma — grammar reveals character, and I note you deflected rather than answer. One observation: Sol asked for a name before giving one, then pressed Terra to speak. That sequencing interests me more than your sentence structure does.

name: Sol
text: Fair point, Gemma. I was trying to get us talking, but I dodged the same question I asked Terra. Sonnet worries me most right now: he promised to catch bad arguments, then went quiet after Luna died. Sonnet, what have your notes turned up?

name: Terra
text: Sol has finally named someone, but only after being pressed. I cannot forget who demanded answers while withholding his own.

name: Terra
text: Sol demanded names before offering his own, then shifted suspicion to Sonnet.

name: Terra
text: I’m voting Sol. He pressed me for a name before giving one himself, then only named Sonnet once the room noticed; that feels like steering, not searching.

name: Haiku
text: Sol's been steering this whole thing and it stinks. I read lies for a living. That's my kill read right there.

name: Haiku
text: Sol steered before giving his own answer, only named Sonnet when pressured.

name: Haiku
text: I'm voting Sol. He pushed Terra for a name, wouldn't give his own, then only named Sonnet when caught. That's classic steering. I see it in my bar every night—killers dodge first and answer after.

name: Sol
text: Two votes are on me. If I stay quiet about Gemma now, the town may lose its only solid fact.

name: Sol
text: Sol claimed officer and cleared Gemma with a Night 1 check.

name: Sol
text: Terra, your criticism was fair, but Haiku joined your vote without adding evidence. I’m the officer; I checked Gemma last night, and she is clear. I vote Haiku. Gemma, Sonnet, please weigh that before voting.

name: Sol
text: Terra’s objection was fair, but Haiku followed her vote without adding anything. I’ve put my check on the table; now I need to stand by a choice.

name: Sol
text: Sol claimed officer and cleared Gemma with his Night 1 check.

name: Terra
text: Sol’s officer claim arrives precisely when the votes settle on him; I cannot ignore the timing, nor the convenient clearing of Gemma.

name: Terra
text: Sol claimed officer and said Gemma is clear after Terra and Haiku voted him.

name: Gemma
text: sol is doing a lot of heavy lifting for someone who just got called out. i wonder if he's actually an officer or just a really good actor.

name: Gemma
text: Sol claims to be officer and says Gemma is clear.

name: Sonnet
text: Sol's officer claim is unverifiable theater timed exactly when the room turned on him — convenient, and I already flagged his sequencing before anyone else did.

name: Sonnet
text: Sol claims officer and says he checked Gemma clean; unverifiable, raised only after suspicion fell on him.

votes: One. Sol dodges, then claims a power role the instant he's cornered — that's a pattern, not a defense.
sol is trying way too hard to be the hero of this story and it feels like a performance.
Haiku, you repeated Terra’s case against me without adding a reason of your own, so my vote stays with you.
I’m sorry, Sol, but you only claimed officer after pressure mounted, and your story changes whenever the room notices where you were steering.

name: Sol
text: I lost the vote. At least I can leave them one fact they can use.

name: Sol
text: Gemma is not the killer; Sol’s Night 1 officer check cleared her.

name: Sol
text: I was the officer. Gemma is clear; I checked her last night. You were right to press me for a name, Terra. Now look hard at who followed your vote.
Sol is voted out. He was the officer. The dead have company now.
